report.tagline: Meta's free AI assistant inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Ray-Ban glasses, now growing into a personal agent called Muse.
report.simpleSummary: Meta AI is the AI helper built into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. You can tap the blue circle or type @Meta AI in a chat to ask questions, make images or plan things with friends. In 2026 Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent app that can do tasks like shopping for you. It is free; Meta makes money mostly from ads, and is starting a paid plan called Muse One.

keyNumbers.note: Up from $19.4 billion a year earlier, mostly AI data centres. Free cash flow turned negative at about minus $2.1 billion.

overview.whatItDoes: Meta AI answers questions, creates images and short videos, edits photos, summarises group chats and helps plan things, all inside apps people already use daily. Muse, launched in 2026, is a more capable agent that can act on your behalf, with shopping as a top activity. Meta does not charge most users; it uses AI to make its apps more engaging and its ads better, and is testing a Muse One subscription.
howItWorks: Tap the Meta AI button or type @Meta AI in a WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger chat.
Meta's own models, built by Meta Superintelligence Labs, write the answer.
Imagine and edit tools make images or change your photos from a prompt.
On Ray-Ban Meta and other smart glasses, you can say 'Hey Meta' and ask about what you see.
The Muse app acts as a personal agent: it remembers your preferences and can shop, compare and book.
Data from your use of Meta AI can be used to personalise content and ads across Meta's apps.
overview.valueProposition: AI help where you already chat, with no new app to download and no cost.

steps.detail: Sees the blue Meta AI circle in WhatsApp.
A chat with Meta AI opens with suggested prompts.
Asks for a Diwali greeting message for customers.
Uses Imagine to create a festive picture.
Forwards the image to family and customer groups.
Uses it again for festivals, quick facts and recipes.
Sees it at the top of the App Store chart.
Links Instagram so Muse learns their style.
'Find a birthday gift for my sister under $80.'
Muse shows three picks with prices and reasons.
Uses Muse again for other purchases and plans.
Asks Meta AI to change the background and lighting.
Shares the post, labelled as AI-edited.

businessModel.summary: Meta AI is free. It makes money indirectly: it keeps people in Meta's apps longer and gives Meta more data to target ads, which are 98 percent of Meta's revenue. Direct revenue is just starting through the Muse One subscription, shopping inside Muse and business AI agents on WhatsApp.

revenueStreams.detail: AI improves recommendations and ad targeting; ad prices rose 14 percent and impressions 10 percent in Q3 2026.
A paid tier for Muse with more capability. Price not confirmed in sources.
Shopping is a top Muse activity, which can bring fees or ads from merchants.
Businesses pay for WhatsApp messages and AI agents that serve customers.

businessModel.pricing: Meta AI and Muse are free to use. Muse One subscription exists; price not public in the sources used.
costDrivers: AI data centres: $34.9 billion of capital spending in Q3 2026 alone
Superintelligence Labs researchers, hired with very large pay packages
Running AI for hundreds of millions of free users
Smart glasses hardware losses in Reality Labs
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Meta AI user pays nothing. Meta earns roughly $50 a year in ads from an average user worldwide, and much more in the US. If Meta AI raises time spent or ad relevance by even a few percent, that adds about $1 to $3 per user per year, which needs to beat the computing cost of their AI use. Muse is costlier because agents use more computing; Meta has said it aims to make Muse about 10 times cheaper to run within a year. These are rough estimates.

growth.moat: Meta's moat is reach and personal data. Billions of people already chat in its apps, and Meta knows their interests from years of activity. A rival can build a smarter chatbot, but it cannot easily get inside WhatsApp.

improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of users who mute Meta AI, and repeat use among those who keep it

improvementIdeas.problem: Small businesses spend hours replying to messages.

pmLessons: Distribution gets trial but not love. Putting a button in front of billions does not mean they will use it.
Forcing a feature on users can hurt trust in the main product.
AI can make money indirectly, through engagement and better ads, before it makes money directly.
When the cost to serve is high, efficiency (like Meta's 10x target for Muse) is a product goal, not just an engineering one.

interviewQuestions.question: Meta AI is in front of billions of people. How would you measure whether it is actually successful?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate exposure from active use. Define a north star around completed tasks. Add guardrails like mute rate and privacy complaints.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Meta make money from Muse?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare subscription, commerce fees and ads. Consider trust risk of ads in an agent. Pick a model and a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Users complain they cannot remove Meta AI from WhatsApp. What would you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh reach versus trust. Propose an opt-out with smart re-entry points. Measure retention of WhatsApp itself.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a Meta AI feature for small businesses in India.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with their pain: answering many messages. Use WhatsApp catalog, UPI payments and Hindi. Define the paid model and success metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Meta is spending $35 billion a quarter on capex. How would you prioritise AI features to justify it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Rank by revenue impact: ad ranking first, then business messaging, then Muse. Explain why and how to measure each.
